tilapia.feedingRatePercentBodyWeight: 2% - 4% depending on fingerling vs grower stage
tilapia.criticalNotes: Tilapia tolerate poor water quality better than carps, but un-ionized ammonia >0.2 mg/L causes branchial hyperplasia and reduces feed conversion ratio.

catfish.criticalNotes: Possesses air-breathing accessory organ, surviving low dissolved oxygen; however highly susceptible to ammonia toxicity, cannibalism during high stocking density, and Columnaris fin erosion.

carp.commonName: Major Indian & Common Carp (Rohu, Catla, Mrigal, Cyprinus carpio)
carp.criticalNotes: Very sensitive to dissolved oxygen dips and gill parasites (Dactylogyrus). Carp surface gasping at dawn requires immediate mechanical aeration.

shrimp.commonName: Pacific White Shrimp / Giant River Prawn (Litopenaeus vannamei / Macrobrachium)
shrimp.criticalNotes: Alkalinity below 100 mg/L causes soft shell syndrome and molt failure. Require vigorous paddlewheel aeration 24/7 during night hours.

diseases.name: White Spot Disease (Ichthyophthiriasis)
symptoms: Small white granular salt-like spots on skin, fins, and gills
Flashing or rubbing sides against pond dykes and nets
Lethargy and loss of appetite
Excess mucus production on skin
treatments: Apply un-iodized coarse pond salt at 2.0 - 3.0 kg per 1,000 liters (2 - 3 ppt) for 7-10 days to disrupt theront stage
Raise water temperature slightly (28°C - 30°C) if controllable to accelerate parasite life cycle
Increase pond aeration and siphon bottom sludge
For nursery tanks: formalin bath at 15-25 ppm under constant strict supervision
diseases.prevention: Quarantine new fingerlings for 14 days; sterilize nets and equipment with potassium permanganate (KMnO4) bath.

diseases.name: Columnaris Disease (Cotton Mouth / Saddleback)
symptoms: White or greyish patches around mouth, head, and dorsal fin ('saddleback')
Frayed, ragged fins with whitish borders
Gill necrosis and pale erosions
Sluggish swimming near the surface
treatments: Immediately lower pond water temperature or shading if heat stressed; stop high-protein feeding
Perform 25% - 30% clean water exchange
Salt bath at 1.0 - 2.0 g/L to relieve osmotic stress
Potassium permanganate (KMnO4) pond treatment at 2 mg/L for open earthen ponds
Consult licensed aquatic veterinarian for oxytetracycline medicated feed if mortality exceeds 5%
diseases.prevention: Avoid rough handling during netting; reduce stocking density; maintain dissolved oxygen above 5.0 mg/L.

diseases.name: Bacterial Hemorrhagic Septicemia & Dropsy
symptoms: Severe abdominal swelling (bloating with ascites fluid)
Protruding pinecone-like scales across flank
Exophthalmia (bulging pop-eyes)
Ulcerative red sores or hemorrhages on belly and fin bases
treatments: Immediately isolate visibly bloated fish to prevent cannibalistic transmission
Halt all feeding for 48 hours to relieve kidney and liver burden
Perform immediate 30% water exchange with conditioned water
Increase dissolved oxygen via auxiliary aerators
Administer veterinary prescribed anti-microbial treatment; sterilize discharge water
diseases.prevention: Never feed spoiled or damp pellets; eliminate organic muck buildup on pond bottom using bio-remediation enzymes.

diseases.name: Ammonia Toxicity / Gill Hyperplasia
diseases.pathogen: Non-infectious (Chemical stress: High pH + elevated Total Ammonia Nitrogen)
symptoms: Fish gasping at surface despite day aeration
Purplish-red or hyperemic inflamed gills with mucus clumps
Erratic darting, corkscrew swimming, spasms
Sudden anorexia (fish refuse feeding pellets completely)
treatments: IMMEDIATE ACTION: Cease 100% of feeding immediately! Unconsumed feed degrades into more toxic ammonia
Perform emergency 30% - 50% bottom water siphon and clean water dilution
Increase mechanical aeration immediately; turbulent air drives off gaseous ammonia
If pH is >8.5, safely buffer down towards 7.5 using humic acids or agricultural gypsum (do not crash pH abruptly)
Add beneficial nitrifying probiotic bacteria (Nitrosomonas/Nitrobacter) to accelerate biological conversion
diseases.prevention: Regularly monitor TAN weekly; calculate un-ionized NH3 with Emerson equation; adhere strictly to feeding tables.

diseases.name: Acute Hypoxia / Dissolved Oxygen Depletion
diseases.pathogen: Environmental (Algal crash, cloudy days, thermal stratification, overfeeding)
symptoms: Mass piping / surface gasping of all fish species, especially at 4:00 AM - 6:00 AM dawn
Fish congregating directly at pond inflows or aerator fountain sprays
Wide open mouths and flared opercula in dead fish
Larger fish dying first before fingerlings
treatments: Turn on ALL aerators, paddlewheels, and water pumps immediately at maximum speed
Pump fresh oxygenated water or spray water as high-pressure fine mist over pond surface
Broadcast sodium percarbonate (emergency chemical oxygen generator) at 5 - 10 kg/hectare if available
Cease all feeding until sunlight restores natural phytoplankton photosynthetic oxygenation
diseases.prevention: Run aerators every night from midnight to sunrise; avoid excess organic fertilizers.

diseases.name: Nitrite Toxicity (Brown Blood Disease)
diseases.pathogen: Chemical stress (Elevated NO2- binding to hemoglobin forming methemoglobin)
symptoms: Chocolate-brown color of gill filaments instead of bright healthy red
Fish behaving hypoxic and sluggish even when dissolved oxygen meter reads normal (>5 mg/L)
Slow swimming at pond margins
treatments: Add agricultural non-iodized salt (NaCl) immediately: Chloride ions (Cl-) competitively block nitrite entry at gill receptors
Target Chloride to Nitrite ratio of at least 10:1 (roughly 50 - 100 kg salt per 100,000 liters for 1 ppm nitrite)
Cease feeding for 24-48 hours
Perform partial water exchange and maximize aeration
diseases.prevention: Avoid premature high stocking before biofilter nitrifying cycle is fully established.

verifiedProcedures.name: Emergency 30% Water Exchange
steps: Drain 25-30% of pond water from bottom drain or submerged siphon to purge anaerobic sludge and organic waste.
Refill gradually with clean, tested, aerated source water over 4-6 hours to prevent temperature shock.
Ensure temperature difference between incoming water and pond is less than 2°C.
Verify pH of new water matches within 0.5 units of pond.

verifiedProcedures.name: Agricultural Liming for Low pH / Low Alkalinity
steps: If pond pH is below 6.5 or total alkalinity is below 60 mg/L CaCO3, apply agricultural limestone (CaCO3) or dolomite.
Standard dose: 200 - 400 kg per hectare (or 20 - 40 g per square meter) dissolved in water slurry and sprayed evenly.
Do not apply quicklime (CaO) or hydrated lime (Ca(OH)2) in stocking ponds with fish, as caustic pH spike (>10.0) causes lethal gill burn.
Recheck pH and alkalinity 24 hours post application.

verifiedProcedures.name: Safe Aquaculture Salt Bath
steps: Use only coarse un-iodized pure rock salt or aquaculture-grade sodium chloride.
For pond-wide application: 1.0 - 3.0 kg per 1,000 liters (1 - 3 ppt). Relieves osmotic stress and prevents nitrite toxicity.
For short dip bath: 10 - 20 g/L for 5 to 10 minutes in a separate quarantine tub under constant aeration. Return fish to pond immediately if they roll over.
